text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--New legal suits against Denmark's leading Danske Bank seem inevitable in connection with the bank's role in the collapse of Hafnia insurance company in 1992. A new legal report sees grounds for compensation. Bankrupt Hafnia was acquired by Codan insurance in 1993.

--Danish finance minister Mogens Lykketoft calls for cuts in tax deductions on mortgages for houseowners in the 1998 state budget or a new tax reform bill. The Central Bank has again warned of an overheating of the economy if Danish private consumption gets out of hand.

--The ruling Social Democrats consider the passage of deregulation laws for the Danish telecoms sector is vital and should be carried out if necessary without the cooperation of the Liberal Party, which is blocking inter-party legislation talks.

--Dansk Supermarked, half-owned by shipping and energy group A.P. Moeller, has bought three container vessels for a total of around one billion crowns, making it one of the country's biggest shippers with a fleet of 18 cargo ships.

--If Denmark upholds its opt-out on joining Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU), Copenhagen risks losing its position as an important regional financial marketplace, Danish Mortgage Bank Association chairman Kjeld Joergensen said at the body's AGM. EMU membership will determine whether Stockholm or Copenhagen becomes the Nordic financial hub, he said.

--Carlsberg-Tetley U.K. brewery managing director Ebbe Dinesen criticised the British monopoly and merger authorities (MMC) for their bureaucratic and slow processing of the planned acquisition of the joint venture by Bass. After eight months, no ruling has been announced.
